# CLI samples for the advanced settings' detection defaults (#367)

What the CLIs really show, for the unit tests (`tests/advanced*.test.ts`) that check Hive's default detection patterns (Settings → Advanced) against them. Each `.txt` is the visible terminal screen, 120 × 40, rendered by `@xterm/headless` from the CLI's output in a pty (rows joined by `\n`, trailing spaces trimmed); folder paths shown on screen are replaced with `C:\work\alpha`.

How they were recorded (12 Oct 2026), each in a new empty folder, with an environment built from an allowlist (no inherited variables). The screens used no sign-in and sent nothing to a real model; the status line is the one exception, below.

- Claude Code: its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set up as `ownClaudeHome()` in `tests/e2e/lib.cjs` does (onboarding done, a made-up API key approved); ended at the question, unanswered. The footers (13 Oct, #696): the same, started with `--permission-mode <mode>`, the trust question (and Bypass permissions' warning) answered Yes, ended at its prompt; the screens show a 401 from loading remote managed settings with the made-up key.
- Codex: the Codex test home (`CODEX_HOME`, `lib.cjs`), in a new `git init` folder it didn't trust (Codex asks only in a Git repository); ended at the question, unanswered, so its `config.toml` was not changed.
- Codex's Full Access warning (17 Oct, #1014): the real Codex suite (`tests/e2e/codex.cjs`, the Codex test home) switching a running agent to Full Access live; rendered with `@xterm/headless` from the terminal's whole output at the pane's size, so the popup is drawn over what was there; answered `1` (its two choices change nothing in the test home); paths replaced with `C:\work\alpha`. Codex prints `Permission selection requested: Full Access` only once the warning is answered.
- Copilot: offline (`COPILOT_OFFLINE=true`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `COPILOT_MODEL=gpt-4.1`) against the stand-in model API (`tests/e2e/fake-copilot-api.cjs`), with `copilotTestEnv()`'s own home, profile and empty `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `gh` off PATH. The footers (13 Oct, #696): the same, started with `--plan`, `--autopilot` or `--allow-all`, the trust question answered Yes, ended at its prompt. The sign-in error used a stand-in of the probe's own that answers every request with 401 and a JSON error body; Copilot reports it as `errorType: "authentication"` (`statusCode: 401`). Its mouse (16 Oct, #737): the same, in a folder its home trusts, started with and without `--no-mouse`, ended at its prompt; for comparison Codex 0.162.1 (the Codex test home, at its prompt) and Claude Code 2.1.301 (its own home, at the trust question) turned on no mouse tracking, so they have no right-click setting. The `--no-mouse` start left `{ "mouse": false }` in that home's `settings.json` (Copilot saves the flag), which is why Hive never passes it.
- Claude Code's mouse at its prompt (21 Oct, #1167): Claude Code 2.1.305 in a 120 × 40 pty, its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set up as `ownClaudeHome()` does, in a new folder; the trust question answered Yes (its default choice is now `No, exit`: Down, then Enter), ended 5 s after its prompt showed, with no prompt sent. It set no mouse tracking (and no alternate screen) at the question or at its prompt.
- Codex's mouse at its prompt (21 Oct, #1167): Codex 0.163.0 in a 120 × 40 pty, the Codex test home, in a new `git init` folder trusted there (`trustForCodex()`), started with `--no-daemon` and a preset's flags (the args in the file), ended 1.5 s after its prompt showed, with no prompt sent. Unlike 0.162.1 (above), it turns on mouse tracking (`?1003h ?1006h`) as it enters the alternate screen.
- Claude Code status line: the signed-in Claude Code test home (`CLAUDE_TEST_HOME`, `lib.cjs`; no API key), `claude --model haiku --settings <file>` whose `statusLine` command dumped its input, one prompt (`say ok`), then `/exit`. Paths are replaced with `C:\work\alpha` (and `C:\work\transcript.jsonl`, `C:\work\scratchpad`), the session and prompt ids with `00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000n`.
- Safeguard stops (#685), the exceptions to the date and the folders: Claude Code's entries and question are #606's, recorded from HB3's real session on 11 Oct (they were in `tests/safeguards.test.ts`, which now reads the question from here). Claude Code's records of a flagged request and Codex's safeguard events have no real recording yet (#697): a name in a CLI's binary isn't one.

Record them again when a CLI's screen changes, named with the new version, and point the tests at them.

The help excerpts (21 Oct, #1167, #1281): each CLI's `--help` with its config folder pointed at a new empty one (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `COPILOT_HOME`), cut down to those options; nothing was written there. Codex's per-tool approval and its listing (21 Oct, #1281): the Codex test home, the screen from a probe's own stdio MCP server in a new trusted folder (gpt-6-luna at low effort, two prompts in all with its control run), rendered as above with the folder replaced by `C:\work\alpha`; the listing with no prompt. Codex's writable roots (23 Oct, #1439): `codex debug prompt-input` (offline) in a new `CODEX_HOME` whose `config.toml` had a root of its own, with `-c sandbox_mode="workspace-write"`, `-c windows.sandbox="unelevated"` and the folder trusted by `-c projects=…` (without them it reads as read-only and names no roots), with and without the `-c` override; and for `--add-dir`, which `prompt-input` doesn't take, one `codex exec` in the Codex test home (one prompt at low effort), its rollout's permissions instructions read back.

The CLIs' exits (26 Oct, HI-1706): a probe of the card's own (in its builder's scratchpad), each CLI in a 120 × 40 pty in a new folder, no prompt sent: Claude Code in its own home as `ownClaudeHome()` sets it up (a made-up API key, no sign-in), the trust question answered Yes (Down, then Enter); Codex in the Codex test home, in a new `git init` folder trusted there (`trustForCodex()`), started with `--no-daemon`. At its prompt the line was typed a key at a time, 30 ms apart, then Enter 300 ms later, as Hive types a slash command; both exited by themselves, with code 0, 1.9 s and 1.4 s after the Enter. Paths replaced with `C:\work\alpha`, Codex's session id with `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`. The real-tier suite `cliquit` checks the same through Hive.

Codex's failed turn (26 Oct, #1658): `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "say ok"` with a new empty `CODEX_HOME` (not the test home) and a model provider of the probe's own (`-c model_providers.standin={…base_url="http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1",wire_api="responses",request_max_retries=0,stream_max_retries=0}`, `model_provider="standin"`): a local stand-in that started the response stream and then dropped the connection. No sign-in, nothing sent to a real model. A provider address refusing connections doesn't fail the turn: Codex waits for the network. Only the two event lines kept.

Values Hive gives a CLI (hook timeouts, Codex's title items and tool timeout) are checked against recordings of the CLI taking them: the hooks arriving (`tests/fixtures/turns-*.json`, `tests/fixtures/console/copilot.json`), Codex's title spinner (`tests/fixtures/codex-startup-0.160.0.json`) and the list above.

Codex's Windows sandbox values (27 Oct, HI-1893) aren't a recording: running Codex's sandbox set off admin prompts on the maintainer's PC (HI-1874), so `windows-sandbox-codex-0.164.0.txt` is an excerpt of Codex's own source at the `rust-v0.164.0` tag (commit `6aaac69480`), the config type that names `unelevated`. Hive's fake-Codex e2e (`connections-codex`) checks the `-c windows.sandbox="unelevated"` it passes; a real run of it belongs in Windows Sandbox.
